title: The Shia adhan
hookLine: many Shia add a testimony that Ali is the wali of Allah in the adhan, which their scholars teach is recommended, not part of the shahada
carry: the call, as each hears it

lines: ALI IS THE WALI OF ALLAH.
cards: Two recordings of the call to prayer, played one after the other. Allahu akbar, in both. I testify that there is no god but Allah, in both.
I testify that Muhammad is the messenger of Allah, in both. Then, in the second recording, a line the first doesn't have: ashhadu anna Aliyyan waliyyullah. I testify that Ali is the wali of Allah.
A listener who grew up with the first call might wonder: is that a third sentence of the shahadah? Today, what Shia Muslims and their scholars say about it.

teach.b: First, who it's about. Ali was the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, Fatima's husband, a figure honored in Sunni and Shia tradition alike.
For Shia Muslims he is also the first imam, the one they hold the Prophet appointed to lead after him. In the Shia call, a line about him comes right after the testimony to the Prophet.
Second, what wali means: a friend, a protector, one close to God. A hadith recorded in Sunni collections, among them Tirmidhi's, has the Prophet say that whoever he is mawla to, Ali is mawla to him.
Mawla, too, can mean friend or protector. Sunni and Shia readers understand that saying differently, and both keep it.
Third, what Shia scholars teach about the line: that it is recommended, and that it is not part of the shahadah. The testimony that makes someone Muslim is still the two sentences of this week.
The line about Ali is said alongside, as an honoring, not as a third pillar of faith.

teach.h: EACH CALL HAS ITS OWN SHAPE.
teach.b: Fourth, each call has its own shape. The Shia call also includes come to the best of deeds. The Sunni dawn call adds a line of its own: prayer is better than sleep.
Each community has its reasons for its wording.
That ends this week: no god, but Allah, the messenger, the new Muslim, the conditions, oneness from three sides, the hidden partner, and now the same testimony, called from two kinds of minaret.

how: In Shia mosques the muezzin often adds ashhadu anna Aliyyan waliyyullah after the testimony to the Prophet and includes hayya 'ala khayr al-'amal; Shia jurists teach the line about Ali is recommended and not part of the adhan's required wording or of the shahadah.

practice: Call to mind any adhan you've heard, even once, even in a film, and hear it slowly in memory, line by line: the greatness, the two testimonies, the invitation to prayer and to success. Notice which line stays with you.
Whether the call you remember is Sunni or Shia, just hear what it carries, without comparing.
